relations.note: Ilya strikes Svyatogor, who pockets Ilya and his horse.
relations.source: Rybnikov and Hilferding northern field records

relations.myth: Sworn brotherhood in the Holy Mountains
relations.note: Svyatogor accepts Ilya as his younger sworn brother and traveling companion.

relations.myth: Transfer of strength from the destined coffin
relations.note: Svyatogor transmits part of his strength to Ilya by breath, foam, sweat, or vapor.
Svyatogor enables Ilya to wield or inherit his sword or weapon.
Svyatogor captains the Falcon Ship while Ilya serves as his esaul.
relations.source: Ilya Muromets with Svyatogor on the Falcon Ship

relations.note: The aged Svyatogor entrusts his sword to Ilya before becoming a mountain.

relations.myth: The bag containing the earth's weight
relations.note: Mikula easily carries the bag that Svyatogor cannot lift.
Mikula directs Svyatogor to the supernatural smith who foretells his marriage.
God causes the unliftable bag to humble Svyatogor's boastful strength.

relations.myth: The angel throws down the earth-weight bag
relations.note: An angel supplies the bag whose weight Svyatogor cannot overcome.
Some songs substitute Samson for Svyatogor or transfer motifs between them.
The personified earth cannot bear Svyatogor and defeats his strength through its weight.
